title: Nearly 60% of Legal Leaders Say AI Adoption is Outpacing Governance, Diligent Institute Report Finds
headline: Nearly 60% of Legal Leaders Say AI Adoption Outpaces Governance
summary: A report by the Diligent Institute and Wilson Sonsini reveals that nearly six in ten legal leaders believe AI adoption is outpacing governance. Furthermore, 41% of respondents lack an established basic AI governance framework, and legal professionals rate their boards' readiness to oversee AI risk at an average of 2.9 out of 5.
why_it_matters: Low board readiness and missing governance frameworks highlight an urgent need for organisations to strengthen AI oversight and involve legal and risk teams earlier in AI deployment decisions.

quotes.text: Nearly six in 10 legal leaders say AI adoption is outpacing governance. That gap is a risk in itself: as AI spreads across an organisation, it becomes harder to maintain clear visibility into how it is used, what data it touches and who is accountable
Boards do not need every director to be an AI expert, but they do need enough fluency to challenge assumptions and ensure oversight keeps pace with adoption.

classification.significance_reason: Provides benchmark data on corporate board readiness and governance gaps in AI adoption from a major governance institute study.
